package_info.package_versions: affected versions served via hijacked S3 bucket (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package delivered binaries from a hijacked S3 bucket, which were replaced with malicious versions that, upon installation or usage, collect user credentials and system information and exfiltrate them to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This behavior is not present in legitimate versions and represents a supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: During npm install or when the package is built/used, specifically at postinstall or build-time
execution_context.file_location: Binary file downloaded from the hijacked S3 bucket, executed via npm postinstall script or invoked during package usage
required_permissions: filesystem (to read credentials and system files)

malicious_snippets.code_language: binary (likely C/C++ or Node.js native addon, actual code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall or build-time, the binary collects user credentials and system information from the filesystem and environment variables, then sends this data via outbound network requests to the attacker's hijacked S3 bucket, resulting in credential and system data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary, instead of performing expected mathematical computations, accesses sensitive files and environment variables to collect credentials and system information, then initiates outbound network connections to an untrusted S3 bucket for data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate bignum binary should only perform mathematical operations and should not access credentials, system information, or make unsolicited network connections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate binaries may collect anonymized telemetry or crash reports, but they do not access credentials or sensitive system files, nor do they exfiltrate such data without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Binary file replaced in S3 bucket without maintainer's authorization
Presence of postinstall script that downloads and executes a remote binary
Unexpected outbound network connections to S3 buckets not associated with the legitimate project
Binary accesses credential files (e.g., ~/.npmrc, environment variables) and system information

attack_chain.action: Attacker hijacks an abandoned S3 bucket previously used by the npm package to serve prebuilt binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binaries are now served to users installing or building the package.

attack_chain.action: User installs or builds the npm package, triggering the download and execution of the malicious binary via a postinstall script or during package usage.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary executes on the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The malicious binary collects user credentials and system information by accessing files and environment variables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is gathered and prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected credentials and system information are exfiltrated via outbound network requests to the attacker's hijacked S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive user data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests to S3 buckets during npm install, build, or postinstall phases
Execution of binaries downloaded from third-party or abandoned cloud storage during package installation
Binaries accessing credential files or environment variables and making outbound network connections
file_indicators: Binaries downloaded from S3 buckets not controlled by the package maintainer (e.g., URLs not matching official project domains)
Presence of npm postinstall scripts that fetch and execute remote binaries
Binary files in node_modules/bignum/bin/ or similar directories that are not present in the official package repository
network_indicators: Outbound connections to S3 buckets or cloud storage endpoints not associated with the legitimate project
Data uploads to S3 buckets with names or ownership not matching the official package maintainers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for postinstall scripts that download and execute binaries from cloud storage, especially S3 buckets. Flag binaries that access credential files or sensitive environment variables and initiate outbound network connections during installation or build. Correlate package metadata and S3 bucket ownership to detect use of abandoned or hijacked buckets. Alert on any network activity to S3 buckets not listed in the official package documentation or repository.
